topics.title: GPS Time Sync Help
topics.body:
GPS Time Sync

GPS Time Sync is a Windows utility for synchronizing the computer clock from a GPS receiver. It was written for use with a VK-172 GPS USB dongle and reads GPS time from NMEA serial data.

Version: 1.20
Primary purpose: keep the system clock accurate using GPS time.

Quick Start

  1. Plug the VK-172 GPS dongle into the computer.
  2. Start GPS Time Sync.
  3. If the GPS receiver is detected, confirm the COM port shown in the COM Port box.
  4. If it is not detected, select the COM port manually.
  5. Confirm the baud rate. The normal value is 9600.
  6. Choose whether to set the Windows clock as Local time or UTC.
  7. Set the sync interval and drift threshold.
  8. Click Save.
GPS reception may take a few moments after plugging in the receiver. Place the receiver where it has a clear view of the sky when possible.

Main Window

The main window shows GPS status, current time, synchronization settings, and logging information.

AreaPurpose
Latitude and LongitudeDisplays the current GPS position when the receiver has a valid fix.
Fix qualityShows the type of GPS fix, such as GPS or DGPS.
Fix modeShows whether GPS data is valid and active.
Satellites in useShows how many satellites are used for the current fix.
Satellites in viewShows how many satellites are visible to the receiver.
Approximate elevationShows the approximate altitude reported by GPS. This value can fluctuate as satellites move.
Current TimeShows the GPS-derived time displayed as local time or UTC depending on the selected setting.
LoggingShows incoming GPS/NMEA lines and application messages.

GPS Receiver and COM Port Setup

GPS Time Sync looks for a VK-172 GPS dongle automatically. If the device is found, the matching COM port is selected. If it is not found, the program lets you select a COM port manually.

SettingRecommended valueNotes
COM PortDetected port, often COM3 or another numbered COM portSelect the port assigned to the GPS receiver.
Baud Rate9600Most VK-172 receivers use 9600 baud.
Enable LoggingOptionalTurn on when diagnosing GPS data or timing problems.
If the selected COM port cannot be opened, another program may be using it, the receiver may be unplugged, or the wrong COM port may be selected.

Synchronization Settings

The Sync Settings panel controls how often the program checks the clock and how much drift is allowed before the Windows clock is updated.

ControlMeaning
Interval (Seconds)How often GPS Time Sync checks the system clock against GPS time. The default is 60 seconds.
Drift >=The number of seconds of difference allowed before the app corrects the system time. The default is 2 seconds.
Set LocalSets the Windows local time based on GPS UTC converted through Windows time zone rules.
Set UTCSets Windows system UTC directly from GPS UTC.
Changing Windows system time may require administrator rights. If time updates fail, run the program as administrator.

Saving Settings

After changing the COM port, baud rate, sync interval, drift threshold, local/UTC mode, or logging option, click Save.

Save applies the current settings and attempts to reopen the selected COM port using the selected baud rate.

Hide to Tray

Click Hide To Tray to keep GPS Time Sync running without leaving the main window open. The tray icon indicates that the program is still active.

Click the tray icon to show the main window again.

Logs

GPS Time Sync can display and write log information for troubleshooting.

LogPurpose
Logging windowShows incoming GPS/NMEA lines and application activity while the program is running.
GPSTimeChange.logRecords startup, shutdown, setting changes, and time correction messages.
gps_sync.logMay be used for GPS synchronization or diagnostic output depending on the installed build.

Logs are normally written beside the application executable.

Understanding GPS Status

Status itemWhat to check
No GPS positionThe receiver may not have a satellite fix yet.
No satellites in useMove the receiver closer to a window or outdoors.
Cannot open COM portChoose the correct COM port, unplug/replug the receiver, or close other software using the port.
Time will not updateRun as administrator and verify that valid GPS time is being received.

Troubleshooting

VK-172 GPS dongle not detected

  • Unplug and reconnect the GPS dongle.
  • Check Windows Device Manager for the assigned COM port.
  • Select the COM port manually in GPS Time Sync.
  • Click Save.

Cannot open COM port

  • Verify the selected COM port.
  • Close other programs that may be using the GPS receiver.
  • Confirm the baud rate is 9600 unless your receiver requires another value.

System time does not change

  • Run GPS Time Sync as administrator.
  • Confirm the GPS receiver has a valid fix.
  • Check the log for error messages.

Displayed elevation changes often

This is normal. GPS elevation can fluctuate due to satellite geometry and signal conditions.

Files and Support Information

FileDescription
GPSTimeSync.exeMain application executable.
gps_settings.iniSaved application settings, when present.
GPSTimeChange.logTime change and application activity log.
EULA.txtLicense terms.
Help folderApplication help files.

Recommended Operating Practice

  • Use the same USB port for the GPS dongle when possible.
  • Verify the COM port after Windows updates or USB device changes.
  • Leave logging off during normal use unless troubleshooting.
  • Run as administrator if the app needs to update Windows system time.
  • Review logs after time synchronization problems.
